<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XVII.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|49}}</noinclude>you? How long shal I suffer you? bring him hither to me. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=18}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} rebuked him, and the deuil vvent out of him, and the ladde vvas cured from that houre. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=19}}† Then came the Disciples to {{sc|Iesvs}} secretely, and said, {{sup|‖}} Why could not we cast him out? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=20}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, because of your incredulity. for, amen I say to you, if you haue {{sup|‖}} faith as a mustard seede, you shal say to this mountaine, Remoue from hence thither: and it shal remoue, and nothing shal be impossible to you. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=21}}† But this kinde is not cast out but by {{sup|‖}} prayer and fasting.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=22}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 9, 31. Luc. 9, 44.''}}* vvhen they conuersed in Galilee, {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, The Sonne of man is to be betraied into the hands of men: {{verse|chapter=17|verse=23}}† and they shal kil him, and the third day he shal rise againe. And they vvere stroken sadde excedingly.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=24}}† And vvhen they vvere come to Capharnaum, there came they that receiued the didrachmes, vnto Peter, and said to him, Your maister doth he not pay the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ These didrachmes were peeces of money which they payed for tribute.}}∷ didrachmes? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=25}}† He saith, Yes. And vvhen he vvas entered into the house, {{sc|Iesvs}} preuented him, saying, What is thy opinion Simon? The kings of the earth of vvhom receiue they tribute or cense? of their children, or of strangers? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=26}}† And he said, Of strangers. {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Then the {{sup|‖}} children are free. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=27}}† But that vve may not scandalize them, goe thy vvaies to the sea, and cast a hooke: and that fish vvhich shal first come vp, take: and vvhen thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This stater was a double didrachme, and therfore was payed for two.}}∷ stater: take that, and giue it them for {{sup|‖}} me and thee.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XVII.}}}}

''2. Transfigured.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Christ can exhibite his body vnder what forme he list.}}Marke in this Transfiguration many maruelous points. as, that he made not only his owne body, which then was mortal, but also the bodies of Moyses and Elias, the one dead, the other to die, for the time as it were immortal: thereby to represent the state and glorie of his body and his Saincts in heauen. By which maruelous transfiguring of his body, you may the lesse maruel that he can exhibite his body vnder the forme of bread and vvine or otherewise as he list.

''3. Appeared Moyses.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Saincts after their death deale with and for the liuing.}}By this that Moyses personally appeared and was present with Christ, it is plaine that the Saincts departed may in person be present at the affaires of the liuing. ''August. de cura pro mort. c. 15. 16''. For euen as Angels els where, so here the Saincts also serued our Sauiour: and therfore as Angels both in the old Testament and the new, were present often at the affaires of men, so may Saincts.

''9. Mount.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Holy places.}}This mount (commonly esteemed and named of the ancient Fathers Thabor) S. Peter {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''2. Pet. 1, 18''.}}calleth ''the holy Mount'' because of this wonderful vision, like as in the old Testament where God appeared to Moyses in the bush, and elsewhere to others, he calleth the place of such Apparitions, ''holy ground'' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 3, 5''.}}. Whereby it is euident that by such Apparitions, places are sanctified, and therevpon groweth a religion and deuotion {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Deuotion and Pilgrimage to the same.}}in the faithful toward such places, and namely to this Mount Thabor (called in S. Hierom ''Itabirium Ep. 17.'' ) there was great Pilgrimage in the Primitiue Church, as vnto al those places which our Sauiour had sanctified with his presence and miracles,<noinclude>{{rh||G|and}}</noinclude>
